Business goal: Create a constrained upload slot so an authorized actor can upload one approved asset without exposing storage internals.
Tenant context rule: Root-owned assets use root context; tenant-scoped assets require exactly one current tenant context; cross-tenant creation denies by default.
Authorization summary: Only actors with the relevant asset-create permission may request an upload intent. The feature validates kind MIME size visibility ownership quota and actor context before allocating a storage key.
Request contract: Body selects asset kind expected content type byte size optional checksum visibility and root or tenant ownership context. Clients must not supply ids storage keys audit fields lifecycle fields or timestamps.
Response contract: Returns asset id upload intent id storage upload target or backend upload instructions expiry and required completion fields. Does not expose permanent bucket authority.
Error contract: 400 invalid kind MIME size checksum quota or system-managed field; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized or cross-tenant context; 409 incompatible visibility or policy; 422 unsupported asset constraints.
Cross-feature seams: None for v1; later consuming features may request scoped intents through the public seam.
Persistence impact: Creates pending asset and upload-intent records with generated storage key and actor/scope binding.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique asset id and upload intent id; unique immutable storage key; indexes on tenant id actor id lifecycle status expiry and upload-intent status.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Upload intent is short-lived single-use actor-bound scope-bound and storage-key-bound.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Expired pending intents cannot be completed; retry creates a new intent and storage key.
Orphaned external resource handling: Cleanup deletes any object present for expired pending intents and marks missing objects honestly.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Support command or minimal scheduler seam; future job platform may take over execution.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Cleanup status and failure reason are recorded for retry when object delete fails.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated root or tenant session depending on ownership scope.
Authorization enforcement layer: Assets feature enforces asset-native authorization tenant boundary quota and upload constraints. Storage adapter remains authz-blind.
Audit requirement: Audit successful and denied upload-intent creation plus quota denials and suspicious repeated attempts.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; filenames content types and asset metadata may contain personal or customer data.
Data classification / PII posture: Asset record must persist PII posture; default unknown or possible unless the approved consumer decision record narrows classification.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when authorized actors can create constrained single-use upload intents and unauthorized quota or cross-tenant attempts are denied before storage keys become usable.

Business goal: Verify that the uploaded object matches its approved intent before an asset becomes usable.
Tenant context rule: Completion must use the same root or tenant context as the upload intent unless an approved internal maintenance context is used.
Authorization summary: Only the actor or approved internal flow associated with the upload intent may complete it. Completion verifies object existence size content type checksum when required expiry and single-use status before changing lifecycle state.
Request contract: Path requires exact asset id. Body supplies upload intent id and optional observed checksum or provider completion data. No mutable asset metadata is accepted.
Response contract: Returns asset metadata with lifecycle and processing status. Assets with no required processing may become ready; assets requiring future processors remain pending processing.
Error contract: 400 invalid asset id or completion payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized or tenant mismatch; 404 asset or intent not found; 409 intent expired already completed or object mismatch; 422 storage verification failed.
Cross-feature seams: Uses storage adapter head or verification seam without leaking storage internals.
Persistence impact: Updates upload intent and asset lifecycle fields plus observed storage metadata and checksum verification status.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index upload intent expiry status and asset id; storage key remains unique.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Completion is the only transition from pending upload to usable lifecycle; failed or mismatched completion does not create a usable asset.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Expired intents cannot be completed; double completion conflicts or is idempotent only for the same verified result if explicitly approved.
Orphaned external resource handling: Mismatched or abandoned uploaded objects are selected for cleanup rather than served.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Support command or minimal scheduler seam handles abandoned completed objects after expiry.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Failed cleanup delete is recorded and retried; checksum mismatch and storage mismatch are durable rejection reasons.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated root or tenant session depending on ownership scope.
Authorization enforcement layer: Assets feature enforces completion ownership tenant boundary lifecycle transitions and storage verification.
Audit requirement: Audit completion failures mismatches checksum failures and successful completions for privileged or tenant-visible assets.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; observed file metadata may contain customer data.
Data classification / PII posture: Completion preserves the asset PII posture from the upload intent or asset record and must not downgrade it automatically.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when an uploaded object cannot become usable unless it matches the approved intent and current actor context.

Business goal: Read policy-filtered asset metadata without exposing raw storage internals.
Tenant context rule: Tenant-scoped reads require current tenant context matching the asset tenant; normal reads exclude deleted assets.
Authorization summary: Actors may read metadata only when asset-native permission and tenant or root scope allow it. Entity-specific reads should normally be mediated by the consuming feature.
Request contract: Path requires exact asset id. No mutable body. Query may later select explicit metadata view only.
Response contract: Returns asset metadata including kind content type byte size checksum visibility lifecycle processing status cleanup status and safe display filename. Does not return private storage credentials.
Error contract: 400 invalid asset id; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized or tenant mismatch; 404 not found or deleted in normal read; 409 asset lifecycle prevents requested view.
Cross-feature seams: Consuming features may call a narrow metadata reader to validate linked assets.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index id tenant id lifecycle status visibility kind and cleanup status.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Normal reads exclude deleted rejected and non-ready assets unless an explicit internal or maintenance view is approved.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Pending rejected and cleanup-failed records remain visible only to explicit maintenance or owner-safe views.
Orphaned external resource handling: No object deletion occurs on metadata read.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: No scheduler dependency for normal reads.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Cleanup failure status may be surfaced to maintenance views without leaking storage credentials.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated root or tenant session depending on ownership scope.
Authorization enforcement layer: Assets feature enforces asset-native read authorization tenant boundary lifecycle and visibility.
Audit requirement: Audit denied metadata reads; successful audit depends on classification of the asset kind and visibility.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; filenames and metadata may reveal personal or customer data.
Data classification / PII posture: Metadata response may expose classification labels to authorized callers and compliance tooling without exposing private storage credentials.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when normal metadata reads are tenant-safe lifecycle-aware and do not expose private storage authority.

Business goal: Surface asset bytes through a policy-aware content seam.
Tenant context rule: Tenant-scoped content reads require current tenant context matching the asset tenant unless the asset is explicitly public and access policy allows public delivery.
Authorization summary: Actors may read content only when asset-native or consuming-feature authorization allows it and the asset is ready visible not deleted and not cleanup-pending.
Request contract: Path requires exact asset id. Read-url body may request an explicit short-lived delivery mode. No broad storage scope may be requested.
Response contract: Returns a same-origin stream or a short-lived signed read URL plus safe content metadata. Private assets never return permanent bucket URLs.
Error contract: 400 invalid asset id or delivery mode; 401 unauthenticated when required; 403 unauthorized tenant mismatch or visibility denial; 404 not found or deleted; 409 asset not ready rejected cleanup-pending or processing-blocked.
Cross-feature seams: Consuming features may call a scoped content-read seam after authorizing entity access.
Persistence impact: Reads durable metadata and delegates byte access to the storage adapter.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index id tenant id lifecycle status visibility processing status and cleanup status.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Content reads are allowed only for ready usable assets unless explicit public policy and processing posture approve otherwise.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Pending upload expired rejected deleted cleanup-pending and processing-blocked assets are not served.
Orphaned external resource handling: No object cleanup occurs on content read; missing storage object should produce typed failure and maintenance signal.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: No scheduler dependency for normal reads.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Missing-object read failures should be recorded for investigation or cleanup follow-up if storage drift is detected.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated root or tenant session for private assets; explicit public policy may allow unauthenticated delivery later.
Authorization enforcement layer: Assets feature enforces asset-native access lifecycle visibility delivery mode and tenant boundary; storage adapter remains authz-blind.
Audit requirement: Audit denied content reads and consider successful reads for sensitive asset classes.
Privacy / personal data impact: High; content may contain personal customer or regulated data.
Data classification / PII posture: Content-read policy must honor the persisted PII posture for audit delivery and future compliance tooling decisions.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when private content is reachable only through policy-aware delivery and raw storage location is not sufficient authority.

Business goal: Soft-delete an asset while preserving durable metadata for audit and compatibility.
Tenant context rule: Tenant-scoped deletes require current tenant context matching the asset tenant; cross-tenant delete denies by default.
Authorization summary: Only actors with delete permission may delete an asset. Deletion refreshes updatedAt sets deletedAt and excludes the asset from normal reads and consumption.
Request contract: Path requires exact asset id. Body is empty or includes explicit deletion reason if approved. Clients cannot supply lifecycle timestamps.
Response contract: Returns deleted asset metadata with deletedAt updatedAt and any deletion or cleanup posture. Object byte deletion or retention policy may be deferred behind storage lifecycle rules.
Error contract: 400 invalid asset id; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized or tenant mismatch; 404 not found; 409 asset already deleted or locked by retention.
Cross-feature seams: Consuming features may request deletion only after entity-specific ownership checks.
Persistence impact: Updates asset lifecycle deletedAt updatedAt and cleanup or retention status; may create audit metadata.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index deletedAt tenant id lifecycle status cleanup status and retention or lock status if added.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Soft delete hides the asset from normal reads and linking; hard byte deletion follows approved retention or cleanup policy.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Deleted records are not normal-read visible; pending byte deletion does not restore usability.
Orphaned external resource handling: Storage object deletion may be immediate for abandoned uploads and deferred or retained for deleted ready assets depending on retention policy.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Support command scheduler or future job platform handles deferred byte deletion if used.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Failed byte deletion is recorded and retried without removing durable asset metadata.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated root or tenant session depending on ownership scope.
Authorization enforcement layer: Assets feature enforces asset-native delete authorization tenant boundary lifecycle and retention rules.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate to high depending on asset content and retention policy.
Data classification / PII posture: Deletion must preserve classification metadata needed for retention audit export and compliance tooling until hard-delete policy allows removal.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when normal reads and linking cannot use deleted assets and deletion does not erase durable facts needed later.

Business goal: Allow consuming features to validate that an asset is usable for a specific entity relationship without importing asset internals.
Tenant context rule: Tenant-scoped validation requires the consuming feature to supply the approved current tenant context and subject reference after it has authorized entity access.
Authorization summary: The consuming feature owns entity-relationship authorization. The assets seam validates tenant match lifecycle readiness visibility kind compatibility cleanup status and deletion status.
Request contract: Input includes asset id tenant or root scope subject type subject id intended role accepted kinds and required readiness level.
Response contract: Returns validation result or throws a typed asset error with reason code. It does not mutate the consuming entity by itself.
Error contract: Invalid asset id subject reference or kind; unauthorized tenant mismatch; not found; deleted; not ready; cleanup pending; incompatible visibility; incompatible kind.
Cross-feature seams: Consumed by future tenant branding web page settings document library and similar features.
Persistence impact: Reads asset metadata and may optionally reserve or link asset depending on approved implementation model.
Indexes / uniqueness: If generic links are added use unique constraints on asset subject role as needed. If explicit foreign keys are used no generic link index is required.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Linked assets must be ready usable and not cleanup-pending unless a consuming-feature decision record explicitly approves another posture.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Expired pending rejected deleted cleanup-pending or processing-blocked assets cannot be linked.
Orphaned external resource handling: No object cleanup occurs on validation; validation can expose maintenance-safe failure reasons.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: No scheduler dependency for validation itself.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Cleanup failures prevent validation for normal consumption until resolved or explicitly waived.
Authentication requirement: Called from already-authenticated feature service context.
Authorization enforcement layer: Consuming feature enforces entity relationship first; assets feature enforces asset invariants second.
Audit requirement: Audit linking attempts when the consuming feature treats the relationship as security or operator relevant.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; links may reveal business relationships and customer content usage.
Data classification / PII posture: Validation must not permit consuming features to ignore or downgrade the asset PII posture defined by the asset record and consumer decision record.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when entity-specific authorization stays in the owning feature and assets remains the invariant guard for asset reuse.

Business goal: Remove cost and lifecycle risk from expired upload intents abandoned pending assets and orphaned storage objects.
Tenant context rule: Maintenance runs outside tenant request context but must process tenant-scoped records without granting cross-tenant read authority to callers.
Authorization summary: Only approved internal maintenance execution or privileged root support may run cleanup. Cleanup changes asset lifecycle and storage object state according to feature-owned rules.
Route(s): Internal maintenance command or support-only route
Request contract: Input selects optional batch size tenant scope dry-run mode and retry-failed-only mode when exposed. Normal clients cannot call this.
Response contract: Returns counts for expired intents rejected assets deleted objects missing objects failed deletes and retry candidates.
Error contract: 400 invalid scope or batch; 401/403 for manual route if exposed; 409 cleanup lock held; 422 storage adapter failure class when batch cannot continue.
Cross-feature seams: Uses storage adapter delete/head operations; future platform scheduler or job platform triggers execution.
Persistence impact: Updates upload intent status asset rejection cleanup status cleanup timestamps and failure reason.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index upload intent expiry status cleanup status tenant id and retry timestamp.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Expired pending uploads are marked rejected and no longer completable; object deletion is attempted if an object exists.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Pending uploads past expiry are abandoned by server-owned cleanup; client cooperation is not required.
Orphaned external resource handling: Objects present for expired pending uploads are deleted; missing objects are recorded as object_missing. Incomplete multipart parts rely on provider lifecycle abort rules.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Support command or minimal scheduler in v1; future job platform may own durable execution retry and observability.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Failed deletes are recorded with retry markers and remain quota/cost-visible until cleanup succeeds or is waived.
Authentication requirement: Internal maintenance context or privileged root support session if exposed manually.
Authorization enforcement layer: Scheduler/job platform owns timing; assets feature owns cleanup semantics lifecycle transitions and storage deletion decisions.
Audit requirement: Audit cleanup runs failed deletes and any manual support invocation.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; cleanup touches customer asset metadata but should not expose content.
Data classification / PII posture: Cleanup must preserve or report classification metadata until durable records are eligible for hard deletion under retention policy.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when expired upload intents cannot become usable and abandoned storage objects have a server-owned cleanup and retry path.

Business goal: Preserve a future worker seam for processors without blocking v1 upload and read foundations.
Tenant context rule: Future jobs must carry an asset id and scope validated by the assets feature; worker execution does not grant cross-tenant authority.
Authorization summary: Future job platform owns queue execution retries and dead-letter behavior. Assets owns processing state transitions cleanup interactions and derived asset or rendition records.
Request contract: Future input includes asset id processor type requested outputs and idempotency key.
Response contract: Future output updates processing status derived metadata and rendition references through an approved assets seam.
Error contract: Future errors include unsupported processor failed processing rejected content retry exhausted cleanup blocked or stale asset version.
Cross-feature seams: Future background job platform and type-specific processors.
Persistence impact: Future processing metadata rendition and processing-cleanup tables may be added.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on processing status processor type asset id pending timestamps and cleanup status when job platform exists.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Processing failures must not leave assets served as ready unless an approved degraded posture exists.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Processing-pending or failed assets remain unavailable for normal consumption when processing is required.
Orphaned external resource handling: Derived objects and failed partial outputs require processor-owned cleanup through assets-approved seams.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Future background job platform owns durable execution retry dead-letter and observability.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Failed derived-object cleanup and processor failures are recorded for retry or operator review.
Authentication requirement: Internal maintenance or worker context plus asset-scoped validation.
Authorization enforcement layer: Job platform enforces execution authority; assets feature enforces asset lifecycle cleanup and update invariants.
Audit requirement: Audit rejected or failed processing for security-sensitive processors such as malware scanning.
Privacy / personal data impact: High for scanned or derived content; processors must not leak private bytes or metadata.
Data classification / PII posture: Processors must preserve or refine PII posture through approved rules and must not downgrade classification without evidence.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable for v1 when the seam is documented but implementation is deferred until the job platform exists.
